name: Al-Furqān
meaning: The Criterion (Al-Furqan - that which clearly separates truth from falsehood, guidance from misguidance, and right from wrong).
revelation_details: Makkan (77 verses, revealed in Makkah during a period of intense mockery, disbelief, and false accusations against Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and the Quran).
core_theme: This Surah is a powerful defense of the Quran and the humanity of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). Revealed when the pagan leaders of Makkah ridiculed the Prophet (pbuh) for being an ordinary human who ate food and walked in the markets, it dismantles every excuse of arrogance, warns against toxic friendships that lead to eternal regret, and closes with a breathtaking portrait of the true "Servants of the Most Merciful" ('Ibad ar-Rahman).
name_origin:
The Surah takes its name from its very first verse: "Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion (Al-Furqan) upon His Servant that he may be to the worlds a warner."

The Historical Context (Separating Truth From Lies): In Makkah, the Quraysh leaders tried every possible tactic to turn people away from Islam. They called the Quran "invented lies" and "tales of the ancients," mocked the Prophet (pbuh) for not being a wealthy king or an angel, and demanded to know why the Quran was not revealed all at once in a single book.

By naming this chapter Al-Furqan (The Criterion), Allah declares that the Quran is the ultimate standard of truth - not only for Makkah, but for all of humanity ("to the worlds"). No matter how loudly people mock or twist reality, Allah's revelation cuts straight through confusion and clearly divides truth from falsehood.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: The Blessed Criterion (Al-Furqan), Allah's Sovereignty, and Helpless False Gods

points.label: The Criterion Sent Down
points.detail: The chapter opens by glorifying Allah, the Blessed One, who sent down Al-Furqan (the Criterion - the Quran, which clearly separates truth from falsehood) upon His servant, Prophet Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم), to be a warner to all the worlds.

points.label: Absolute Sovereignty
points.detail: To Allah alone belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He has never taken a son, has no partner in His rule, and created every single thing in exact, precise measure.

points.label: Helplessness of Idols
points.detail: Despite this, people take false gods besides Allah that cannot create anything - rather, they are themselves created - and possess no power to bring harm or benefit, nor control over death, life, or resurrection.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• The Criterion Sent Down: The chapter opens by glorifying Allah, the Blessed One, who sent down Al-Furqan (the Criterion - the Quran, which clearly separates truth from falsehood) upon His servant, Prophet Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم), to be a warner to all the worlds.
• Absolute Sovereignty: To Allah alone belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He has never taken a son, has no partner in His rule, and created every single thing in exact, precise measure.
• Helplessness of Idols: Despite this, people take false gods besides Allah that cannot create anything - rather, they are themselves created - and possess no power to bring harm or benefit, nor control over death, life, or resurrection.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Classical scholars like Ibn Kathir note that referring to Prophet Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم) as 'Abdihi (His servant) in verse 1 honors his deep humility and servitude to Allah. Calling the Quran Al-Furqan (the Criterion) sets the theme of the entire Surah: providing a clear, unshakable standard that separates true faith from false excuses and empty worship.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: False Accusations Against the Quran and Mocking a Human Messenger

points.label: Accusations of Fabrication
points.detail: The disbelievers dismiss the Quran as a lie invented by the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) with the help of others, calling it "legends of the former peoples" that he had written down morning and evening.

points.label: The Divine Reply
points.detail: Allah commands the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) to reply that the Quran was sent down by the One who knows every secret in the heavens and the earth, and He is Forgiving and Merciful.

points.label: Mocking His Humanity
points.detail: The arrogant leaders ask: "What kind of messenger is this who eats food and walks in the markets? Why was an angel not sent down with him, or a treasure handed to him, or a private garden to eat from?" They even claim the believers are merely following a "bewitched man.

points.label: Lost in Contradictions
points.detail: Allah notes how they invent wild, contradictory labels for the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم), leaving themselves completely astray and unable to find the right path.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• Accusations of Fabrication: The disbelievers dismiss the Quran as a lie invented by the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) with the help of others, calling it "legends of the former peoples" that he had written down morning and evening.
• The Divine Reply: Allah commands the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) to reply that the Quran was sent down by the One who knows every secret in the heavens and the earth, and He is Forgiving and Merciful.
• Mocking His Humanity: The arrogant leaders ask: "What kind of messenger is this who eats food and walks in the markets? Why was an angel not sent down with him, or a treasure handed to him, or a private garden to eat from?" They even claim the believers are merely following a "bewitched man."
• Lost in Contradictions: Allah notes how they invent wild, contradictory labels for the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم), leaving themselves completely astray and unable to find the right path.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Tafsir scholars explain that the Makkan elites judged prophethood by worldly luxury - expecting a messenger to be a wealthy king with gold palaces or an angel detached from human life. Yet Allah sent a human messenger who ate, worked, and walked through ordinary markets so that everyday people could relate to him and follow his practical example.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Allah's Greater Reward and the Terrifying Reality of Hellfire

points.label: Better Than Worldly Treasures
points.detail: Allah reminds the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) that if He willed, He could easily grant him far better than the gardens and palaces the disbelievers demanded - gardens with flowing rivers and grand palaces.

points.label: The Real Reason for Rejection
points.detail: Their real issue is not a lack of proof; they simply deny the Final Hour. For those who deny the Hour, Allah has prepared a blazing Fire.

points.label: The Roaring Fire
points.detail: When Hellfire sees them from a distance, they will hear its furious raging and roaring. When they are thrown chained together into a tight, narrow space within it, they will cry out for destruction - only to be told: "Do not cry out today for one destruction, but cry out for many destructions!

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• Better Than Worldly Treasures: Allah reminds the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) that if He willed, He could easily grant him far better than the gardens and palaces the disbelievers demanded - gardens with flowing rivers and grand palaces.
• The Real Reason for Rejection: Their real issue is not a lack of proof; they simply deny the Final Hour. For those who deny the Hour, Allah has prepared a blazing Fire.
• The Roaring Fire: When Hellfire sees them from a distance, they will hear its furious raging and roaring. When they are thrown chained together into a tight, narrow space within it, they will cry out for destruction - only to be told: "Do not cry out today for one destruction, but cry out for many destructions!
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Classical commentators like Ibn Kathir point out the striking contrast between the cramped, suffocating darkness of Hell and the wide, peaceful freedom of Paradise. People who felt "too big" and arrogant to submit to Allah in this world will find themselves confined in the tightest, most humiliating place in the Hereafter.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Eternal Paradise vs. False Gods Disowning Their Worshippers

points.label: The Garden of Eternity
points.detail: Allah asks directly: Is that terrifying Fire better, or the Garden of Eternity promised to those with taqwa (mindfulness of Allah)? There, they will have everything they desire forever - a binding promise from their Lord.

points.label: False Gods Speak Out
points.detail: On the Day of Judgment, Allah will gather the polytheists along with everything they worshipped besides Him, and ask those worshipped beings: "Did you mislead these servants of Mine, or did they stray from the path themselves?

points.label: Total Disavowal
points.detail: They will reply: "Glory be to You! It was never right for us to take any protectors besides You. Rather, You gave them and their fathers worldly enjoyment until they forgot the Reminder and became a ruined people." Thus, their own objects of worship will expose their lies, leaving them with no escape and no helper.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• The Garden of Eternity: Allah asks directly: Is that terrifying Fire better, or the Garden of Eternity promised to those with taqwa (mindfulness of Allah)? There, they will have everything they desire forever - a binding promise from their Lord.
• False Gods Speak Out: On the Day of Judgment, Allah will gather the polytheists along with everything they worshipped besides Him, and ask those worshipped beings: "Did you mislead these servants of Mine, or did they stray from the path themselves?"
• Total Disavowal: They will reply: "Glory be to You! It was never right for us to take any protectors besides You. Rather, You gave them and their fathers worldly enjoyment until they forgot the Reminder and became a ruined people." Thus, their own objects of worship will expose their lies, leaving them with no escape and no helper.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Tafsir scholars explain that verse 18 reveals a major root cause of spiritual ruin: excessive worldly comfort (mata') without gratitude. When people become absorbed in ease and luxury, they gradually forget Allah's Reminder until they lose their way completely.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: All Messengers Were Human and People Are a Test for One Another

points.label: Every Messenger Was Human
points.detail: Allah affirms that every messenger sent before Prophet Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم) also ate food and walked in the markets.

points.label: Testing Each Other
points.detail: Allah declares a universal law of life: "And We have made some of you a trial (fitnah) for others - will you have patience? And your Lord is ever All-Seeing.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• Every Messenger Was Human: Allah affirms that every messenger sent before Prophet Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم) also ate food and walked in the markets.
• Testing Each Other: Allah declares a universal law of life: "And We have made some of you a trial (fitnah) for others - will you have patience? And your Lord is ever All-Seeing.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Classical scholars like Al-Qurtubi and Ibn Kathir explain that this single verse holds profound wisdom for human society: the rich are a test for the poor, the healthy for the sick, the strong for the weak, and the disbelievers for the believers. Every relationship and hardship is a test of our patience (sabr), comforted by the closing reminder that Allah sees everything we endure.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Arrogant Demands to See Angels and Worthless Deeds Turned to Dust

points.label: Arrogant Demands
points.detail: Those who do not expect to meet Allah arrogantly ask, "Why are angels not sent down to us, or why do we not see our Lord?" They have become deeply arrogant within themselves and crossed all bounds.

points.label: The Day They Finally See Angels
points.detail: On the Day they actually see the angels (at death and on Judgment Day), there will be no good news for the criminals - the angels will declare a complete barrier (hijran mahjura) keeping them away from mercy and Paradise.

points.label: Deeds Turned to Dust
points.detail: Allah will turn to all the worldly deeds they did and scatter them like fine dust floating in the air (haba'an manthura).

points.label: The Best Resting Place
points.detail: In contrast, the people of Paradise on that Day will have the finest home and the most peaceful resting place.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• Arrogant Demands: Those who do not expect to meet Allah arrogantly ask, "Why are angels not sent down to us, or why do we not see our Lord?" They have become deeply arrogant within themselves and crossed all bounds.
• The Day They Finally See Angels: On the Day they actually see the angels (at death and on Judgment Day), there will be no good news for the criminals - the angels will declare a complete barrier (hijran mahjura) keeping them away from mercy and Paradise.
• Deeds Turned to Dust: Allah will turn to all the worldly deeds they did and scatter them like fine dust floating in the air (haba'an manthura).
• The Best Resting Place: In contrast, the people of Paradise on that Day will have the finest home and the most peaceful resting place.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Ibn Kathir and As-Sa'di note that good deeds require two conditions to be accepted by Allah: sincerity for His sake alone and following His guidance. Without faith in Allah, even outwardly impressive acts lose their spiritual weight on Judgment Day, vanishing like dust in a beam of sunlight.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: The Sky Splitting, Biting One's Hands in Regret, and Abandoning the Quran

points.label: A Hard Day for Disbelievers
points.detail: On the Day the sky splits open with clouds and the angels descend in continuous ranks, true sovereignty will belong solely to Ar-Rahman (the Most Merciful) - a terribly hard Day for the disbelievers.

points.label: Biting One's Hands in Regret
points.detail: On that Day, the wrongdoer will bite his own hands in agony, crying: "Oh, I wish I had taken a path with the Messenger! Woe to me! I wish I had never taken so-and-so as a close friend! He led me astray from the Reminder after it had come to me." And Shaytan has always deserted humanity in their hour of need.

points.label: The Prophet's Complaint (Verse 30)
points.detail: On that Day, the Messenger (صلى الله عليه وسلم) will say: "O my Lord, indeed my people have taken this Quran as a thing abandoned (mahjura).

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• A Hard Day for Disbelievers: On the Day the sky splits open with clouds and the angels descend in continuous ranks, true sovereignty will belong solely to Ar-Rahman (the Most Merciful) - a terribly hard Day for the disbelievers.
• Biting One's Hands in Regret: On that Day, the wrongdoer will bite his own hands in agony, crying: "Oh, I wish I had taken a path with the Messenger! Woe to me! I wish I had never taken so-and-so as a close friend! He led me astray from the Reminder after it had come to me." And Shaytan has always deserted humanity in their hour of need.
• The Prophet's Complaint (Verse 30): On that Day, the Messenger (صلى الله عليه وسلم) will say: "O my Lord, indeed my people have taken this Quran as a thing abandoned (mahjura).
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Classical commentators explain that verses 27-29 were revealed regarding Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt, who nearly embraced Islam until his bad friend Ubayy ibn Khalaf pressured him into rejecting and insulting the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) - serving as a timeless warning about how toxic friendships can ruin a person's eternal life. Meanwhile, Ibn Kathir lists several ways people "abandon" the Quran in verse 30: refusing to listen to it, failing to recite or reflect on it, ignoring its commands and prohibitions, and not seeking healing or guidance from it.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Enemies of Every Prophet and the Wisdom of Gradual Revelation

points.label: Every Prophet Had Enemies
points.detail: Allah comforts the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) that every earlier prophet was given enemies from among the criminals, and Allah is fully sufficient as a Guide and Helper.

points.label: Why the Quran Was Revealed Gradually
points.detail: The disbelievers asked, "Why was the Quran not sent down to him all at once in a single book?" Allah explains the deep wisdom: it was revealed gradually in stages "so that We may strengthen your heart with it," and recited in clear, measured portions.

points.label: The Best Answer
points.detail: No objection or trick do they bring except that Allah sends down the clear truth and the finest explanation in response. Those who are dragged on their faces into Hell will be in the worst position and furthest astray.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• Every Prophet Had Enemies: Allah comforts the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) that every earlier prophet was given enemies from among the criminals, and Allah is fully sufficient as a Guide and Helper.
• Why the Quran Was Revealed Gradually: The disbelievers asked, "Why was the Quran not sent down to him all at once in a single book?" Allah explains the deep wisdom: it was revealed gradually in stages "so that We may strengthen your heart with it," and recited in clear, measured portions.
• The Best Answer: No objection or trick do they bring except that Allah sends down the clear truth and the finest explanation in response. Those who are dragged on their faces into Hell will be in the worst position and furthest astray.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Tafsir scholars highlight the tender mercy in verse 32: revealing the Quran over 23 years continually comforted, strengthened, and guided Prophet Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم) and the companions through every crisis, battle, and question as it happened - making the Quran a living companion rather than a distant, static text.

points.label: Musa and Harun (AS)
points.detail: Allah gave Prophet Musa (AS) the Book and appointed his brother Harun (AS) as his helper, sending them to Pharaoh's people who denied Allah's signs and were completely destroyed.

points.label: Nuh, 'Ad, Thamud, and Ar-Rass
points.detail: When the people of Prophet Nuh (AS) rejected the messengers, Allah drowned them and made them a sign for humanity. The same fate befell 'Ad, Thamud, the Companions of the Well (Ashab ar-Rass), and many generations in between - each given clear warnings before being utterly ruined.

points.label: Passing by the Ruins of Lut's Town
points.detail: The pagan Quraysh regularly traveled right past the destroyed town of Prophet Lut's people, upon which Allah rained a terrible rain of stones - yet they failed to take a lesson because they refused to expect Resurrection.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• Musa and Harun (AS): Allah gave Prophet Musa (AS) the Book and appointed his brother Harun (AS) as his helper, sending them to Pharaoh's people who denied Allah's signs and were completely destroyed.
• Nuh, 'Ad, Thamud, and Ar-Rass: When the people of Prophet Nuh (AS) rejected the messengers, Allah drowned them and made them a sign for humanity. The same fate befell 'Ad, Thamud, the Companions of the Well (Ashab ar-Rass), and many generations in between - each given clear warnings before being utterly ruined.
• Passing by the Ruins of Lut's Town: The pagan Quraysh regularly traveled right past the destroyed town of Prophet Lut's people, upon which Allah rained a terrible rain of stones - yet they failed to take a lesson because they refused to expect Resurrection.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Classical commentators point out how Allah reminds the Makkans of ruins they literally walked past on their trade caravans to Syria. Looking at history with an arrogant heart produces blindness, whereas a reflective heart sees past ruins as urgent reminders to turn back to Allah.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Mocking the Prophet and Worshipping One's Own Desires

points.label: Mockery of the Messenger
points.detail: Whenever the disbelievers see the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم), they mock him: "Is this the one Allah sent as a messenger? He almost misled us from our gods if we had not stayed patient with them!" Soon, when they see the punishment, they will know who was truly astray.

points.label: Worse Than Cattle
points.detail: Do you think most of them truly listen or use their reason? They are only like grazing cattle - in fact, even further astray from the right path.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• Mockery of the Messenger: Whenever the disbelievers see the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم), they mock him: "Is this the one Allah sent as a messenger? He almost misled us from our gods if we had not stayed patient with them!" Soon, when they see the punishment, they will know who was truly astray.
• Worshipping Desires (Hawa): Allah asks: "Have you seen the one who takes his own desire as his god?" The Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) cannot force such a person to be guided.
• Worse Than Cattle: Do you think most of them truly listen or use their reason? They are only like grazing cattle - in fact, even further astray from the right path.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Kathir explain that verse 43 exposes the most subtle form of idolatry: making one's own whims and desires (hawa) the ultimate authority - doing whatever feels good and rejecting whatever restricts one's ego. Cattle at least follow the natural instinct Allah gave them, whereas a human who ignores his intellect to chase blind desires falls even lower.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Signs in Nature - Shadows, Night, Sleep, Winds, and Pure Rain

points.label: The Moving Shadow
points.detail: Look at how Allah stretches out the shadow - if He willed, He could have frozen it in place - yet He made the sun its guide and gradually draws it back in.

points.label: Night, Sleep, and Day
points.detail: Allah made the night a comforting covering (libas), sleep a quiet rest (subat), and the day a time to rise and work.

points.label: Winds and Pure Rain
points.detail: Allah sends the winds as glad tidings before His mercy and sends down pure, purifying water (ma'an tahura) from the sky to bring dead land back to life and give drink to countless animals and humans. Allah distributes this rain across lands so people may remember and be grateful, yet most people insist on ingratitude.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• The Moving Shadow: Look at how Allah stretches out the shadow - if He willed, He could have frozen it in place - yet He made the sun its guide and gradually draws it back in.
• Night, Sleep, and Day: Allah made the night a comforting covering (libas), sleep a quiet rest (subat), and the day a time to rise and work.
• Winds and Pure Rain: Allah sends the winds as glad tidings before His mercy and sends down pure, purifying water (ma'an tahura) from the sky to bring dead land back to life and give drink to countless animals and humans. Allah distributes this rain across lands so people may remember and be grateful, yet most people insist on ingratitude.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Tafsir scholars admire how Allah turns everyday experiences - the gentle movement of a shadow, the relief of a good night's sleep, and fresh rain falling on dry soil - into unmistakable proofs of His mercy and precision. Calling sleep a "rest" and waking up a "resurrection" (nushur) also serves as a daily mini-reminder of death and the Day of Judgment.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Striving With the Quran, the Two Seas, and Human Creation

points.label: Strive With the Quran
points.detail: Had Allah willed, He could have sent a separate warner to every single town, yet He honored Prophet Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم) as the universal messenger. Allah commands him not to give in to the disbelievers, and to strive against them with the Quran in a great striving (jihadan kabira).

points.label: The Barrier Between Two Seas
points.detail: Allah released the two bodies of water - one fresh and sweet, the other salty and bitter - and placed an unseen barrier (barzakh) and partition between them so they do not overwhelm one another.

points.label: Human Creation and Family Ties
points.detail: Allah created humanity from water and established blood relationships and marriage ties - showing His complete power. Yet disbelievers still worship helpless things that can neither benefit nor harm them.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• Strive With the Quran: Had Allah willed, He could have sent a separate warner to every single town, yet He honored Prophet Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم) as the universal messenger. Allah commands him not to give in to the disbelievers, and to strive against them with the Quran in a great striving (jihadan kabira).
• The Barrier Between Two Seas: Allah released the two bodies of water - one fresh and sweet, the other salty and bitter - and placed an unseen barrier (barzakh) and partition between them so they do not overwhelm one another.
• Human Creation and Family Ties: Allah created humanity from water and established blood relationships and marriage ties - showing His complete power. Yet disbelievers still worship helpless things that can neither benefit nor harm them.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Classical scholars like Ibn Abbas explain that "strive against them with it (the Quran) a great striving" in verse 52 means using the Quran's clear proofs, wisdom, and message to confront falsehood with patience and conviction. Meanwhile, mentioning both fresh/salty waters and blood/marriage ties highlights how Allah designed both nature and human families in perfect harmony.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: The Prophet's Mission, Trusting the Ever-Living, and Ar-Rahman

points.label: No Worldly Payment
points.detail: The Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) was sent strictly as a bringer of good news and a warner, asking for no payment - only that whoever wishes may take a path back to their Lord.

points.label: Rely on the Ever-Living
points.detail: Allah commands: "And put your trust (tawakkul) in the Ever-Living (Al-Hayy) who never dies, and glorify His praise." He is fully aware of His servants' sins.

points.label: Creator of the Universe
points.detail: He created the heavens, the earth, and everything between them in six days, then rose over the Throne - Ar-Rahman (the Most Merciful).

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• No Worldly Payment: The Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) was sent strictly as a bringer of good news and a warner, asking for no payment - only that whoever wishes may take a path back to their Lord.
• Rely on the Ever-Living: Allah commands: "And put your trust (tawakkul) in the Ever-Living (Al-Hayy) who never dies, and glorify His praise." He is fully aware of His servants' sins.
• Creator of the Universe: He created the heavens, the earth, and everything between them in six days, then rose over the Throne - Ar-Rahman (the Most Merciful).
• Refusing to Prostrate to Ar-Rahman: When the disbelievers are told, "Prostrate to Ar-Rahman," they arrogantly reply, "And what is Ar-Rahman? Should we prostrate to whatever you command us?" - increasing only in aversion. (Verse 60 is a verse of Prostration / Sajdah).
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Tafsir scholars highlight the immense strength in verse 58: human supporters, wealth, and status all eventually fade or die, so placing one's ultimate reliance (tawakkul) in Al-Hayy - the Ever-Living who never dies - gives a believer unshakable peace and courage.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Constellations in the Sky and the Alternating Night and Day

points.label: The Adorned Sky
points.detail: Blessed is Allah who placed great constellations (buruj) in the sky, and placed within it a burning lamp (the sun) and a glowing, luminous moon.

points.label: A Daily Chance for Gratitude
points.detail: He made the night and the day follow one another in constant succession specifically for anyone who wishes to remember Allah or wishes to be grateful.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• The Adorned Sky: Blessed is Allah who placed great constellations (buruj) in the sky, and placed within it a burning lamp (the sun) and a glowing, luminous moon.
• A Daily Chance for Gratitude: He made the night and the day follow one another in constant succession specifically for anyone who wishes to remember Allah or wishes to be grateful.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Classical commentators explain that verse 62 offers a beautiful, practical spiritual lesson: if a believer misses a good deed or act of worship during the day, the night arrives as a fresh chance to make it up - and if they miss it at night, the day arrives as another opportunity to remember and thank Allah.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: The Servants of the Most Merciful ('Ibad ar-Rahman) - Humility, Prayer, and Balance

points.label: Humility and Peace
points.detail: The true servants of Ar-Rahman walk upon the earth gently and humbly (hawnan), without arrogance. When ignorant people address them with harsh or foolish words, they respond with words of peace (Salaman) and walk away with dignity.

points.label: Devotion in the Night
points.detail: They spend part of the night in prostration and standing in prayer before their Lord.

points.label: Fear of Hellfire
points.detail: Despite their worship, they remain humble and pray: "Our Lord, avert from us the punishment of Hell; indeed, its punishment is an unending torment. Indeed, it is an evil settlement and resting place.

points.label: Balanced Spending
points.detail: When they spend, they are neither wasteful nor stingy, but hold a firm, balanced middle path between the two.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• Humility and Peace: The true servants of Ar-Rahman walk upon the earth gently and humbly (hawnan), without arrogance. When ignorant people address them with harsh or foolish words, they respond with words of peace (Salaman) and walk away with dignity.
• Devotion in the Night: They spend part of the night in prostration and standing in prayer before their Lord.
• Fear of Hellfire: Despite their worship, they remain humble and pray: "Our Lord, avert from us the punishment of Hell; indeed, its punishment is an unending torment. Indeed, it is an evil settlement and resting place."
• Balanced Spending: When they spend, they are neither wasteful nor stingy, but hold a firm, balanced middle path between the two.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Right after the disbelievers mocked the name Ar-Rahman in verse 60, Allah honors His true believers by attaching them directly to that very name: 'Ibad ar-Rahman ("Servants of the Most Merciful"). Ibn Kathir notes that their humility is not weakness - it is calm self-control, refusing to sink to the level of insults and maintaining moderation in both worship and finances.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Avoiding Major Sins and Turning Evil Deeds Into Good Deeds

points.label: Staying Clear of Three Major Sins
points.detail: They never invoke any other deity alongside Allah, never kill a soul Allah has made sacred except by rightful justice, and never commit zina (unlawful sexual relations). Whoever commits these faces doubled punishment and lasting humiliation on the Day of Resurrection.

points.label: The Miracle of Sincere Repentance (Verse 70)
points.detail: An extraordinary exception is given to "whoever repents, believes, and does righteous work - for them, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds (yubaddilullahu sayyi'atihim hasanat)." Truly, Allah is Oft-Forgiving and Most Merciful.

points.label: Returning to Allah
points.detail: Whoever repents and does good has truly returned to Allah in the finest way.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
• Staying Clear of Three Major Sins: They never invoke any other deity alongside Allah, never kill a soul Allah has made sacred except by rightful justice, and never commit zina (unlawful sexual relations). Whoever commits these faces doubled punishment and lasting humiliation on the Day of Resurrection.
• The Miracle of Sincere Repentance (Verse 70): An extraordinary exception is given to "whoever repents, believes, and does righteous work - for them, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds (yubaddilullahu sayyi'atihim hasanat)." Truly, Allah is Oft-Forgiving and Most Merciful.
• Returning to Allah: Whoever repents and does good has truly returned to Allah in the finest way.
verse_breakdowns.reflection: Verse 70 is one of the most hopeful verses in the entire Quran. In an authentic Hadith recorded in Sahih Muslim (190a), Abu Dharr (RA) narrated that the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) described a man on Judgment Day whose minor sins are shown to him, and then Allah announces: "For every evil deed you committed, you now have a good deed!" - causing the man to joyfully ask about his major sins as well. No past mistake is too big for Allah's mercy when a person sincerely repents and changes their life.

verse_breakdowns.reflection: Classical scholars like Al-Hasan al-Basri explained that "comfort to our eyes" in verse 74 means seeing one's spouse and children happily obeying Allah - bringing the deepest possible joy to a believer's heart. Closing the entire Surah with verse 77 reminds every human being of their true worth: our real value in the sight of Allah comes from our worship, humility, and turning to Him in du'a.

stories_in_surah.title: The Epic Stories, Events, and Scenes of Surah Al-Furqan
stories_in_surah.content: According to classical scholars of Tafsir (such as Ibn Kathir, Al-Tabari, and Al-Baghawi) and authentic Hadith collections, these are the detailed accounts of the major events, historical lessons, and vivid scenes found in this chapter:

stories_in_surah.title: The Day of Bitter Regret: The Story of Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt (Verses 27-29)
stories_in_surah.content:
This is one of the most chilling warnings about bad friendship in the entire Quran: "And the Day the wrongdoer will bite on his hands [in regret] he will say, 'Oh, I wish I had taken with the Messenger a way! Oh, woe to me! I wish I had not taken that one as a friend! He led me away from the Reminder after it had come to me.'"

The Tafsir Details: Classical Tafsir scholars (including Ibn Kathir, Al-Tabari, and Al-Baghawi) preserve the heartbreaking real-life story behind these verses. Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt was a nobleman of Makkah who used to host feasts and sit with Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). One day, he invited the Prophet (pbuh) to a feast, and the Prophet (pbuh) gently said he would not eat until Uqbah testified that there is no true god except Allah and that Muhammad is His Messenger. Uqbah actually pronounced the testimony of faith!

However, Uqbah had a toxic close friend - Ubayy ibn Khalaf (or Umayyah ibn Khalaf in another narration), a bitter enemy of Islam. When Ubayy heard what happened, he shamed Uqbah and swore he would never speak to him again unless Uqbah went back, insulted the Prophet (pbuh), and spat in his face. Tragically, Uqbah cared more about pleasing his friend than pleasing Allah - he walked away from Islam and committed that shameful act.

Both men later died as disbelievers (Uqbah was executed after being captured at the Battle of Badr, and Ubayy was killed at the Battle of Uhud). Their story serves as an eternal warning for every person: choosing a toxic friend over Allah's guidance leads to biting one's own hands in unbearable regret on Judgment Day, when Shaytan completely abandons those he misled.

stories_in_surah.title: The Prophet's Complaint: Abandoning the Quran (Verse 30)
stories_in_surah.content:
Immediately after the scene of regret on Judgment Day, Allah records a deeply sobering moment: "And the Messenger has said, 'O my Lord, indeed my people have taken this Quran as [a thing] abandoned (mahjura).'"

The Tafsir Details: Classical commentators like Ibn Kathir explain that abandoning the Quran (hajr al-Quran) happened in Makkah when the polytheists refused to listen to it, made loud noise while it was recited, and refused to believe in it. Yet scholars also remind believers that abandoning the Quran takes several forms in everyday life:

• Refusing to read or recite it.
• Reading it without reflecting on its meaning.
• Knowing its teachings but refusing to live by its commands.

This single verse is a gentle, powerful wake-up call for every believer to keep the Quran alive in their heart, home, and daily actions.

stories_in_surah.title: Past Destroyed Nations and the People of Ar-Rass (Verses 35-40)
stories_in_surah.content:
To remind the Quraysh that mocking messengers always ends in destruction, Allah briefly walks through a gallery of earlier nations.

The Tafsir Details: Allah mentions sending Prophet Musa (AS) with his brother Harun (AS) as a helper to Pharaoh's people, who rejected Allah's signs and were utterly destroyed. Next, He recalls the people of Prophet Nuh (AS), who drowned in the great flood and became a lasting sign for humanity.

Allah then lists three other vanished communities: the mighty tribe of 'Ad, the tribe of Thamud, and the Companions of Ar-Rass (Ashab ar-Rass), along with many generations in between. Classical scholars (like Ibn Kathir, citing Ibn Abbas and Ikrimah) explain that Ar-Rass refers to a well - either a village belonging to the remnants of Thamud or a people who killed their prophet and threw him into a deep well - after which Allah wiped them out completely. Finally, Allah points directly to the ruined town of Prophet Lut (AS), reminding the Quraysh that they literally walk right past those ruins on their trade journeys, yet they still refuse to expect the Resurrection.

deep_dives.title: The Unique Status of the Surah (The Seven Modes of Recitation)
deep_dives.content:
Surah Al-Furqan is the exact chapter involved in one of the most famous authentic Hadiths about how the Quran was revealed to make recitation easy for all tribes and peoples.

In an authentic Hadith narrated by Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) and recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari (4992, 5041) and Sahih Muslim (818a), Umar (RA) overheard a companion named Hisham ibn Hakim (RA) reciting Surah Al-Furqan in prayer in a dialect/style different from the way Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) had taught Umar (RA). Umar nearly interrupted his prayer out of shock, waited impatiently until Hisham finished, grabbed him by his cloak, and brought him straight to the Prophet (pbuh).

The Prophet (pbuh) asked Hisham (RA) to recite, and then said: "Thus it was revealed." Then he asked Umar (RA) to recite, and again said: "Thus it was revealed." Finally, the Prophet (pbuh) taught them a foundational truth of Quranic preservation: "Indeed, this Quran has been revealed in seven different modes (Ahruf), so recite of it whichever is easiest for you.

deep_dives.title: The Mockery of the Quraysh and Why the Quran Came Gradually (Verses 4-9, 32-33)
deep_dives.content:
Early in the Surah, Allah records the exact sarcastic objections raised by the pagan leaders of Makkah and answers them one by one.

The Tafsir Details: The disbelievers accused Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) of making up the Quran with the help of others, claiming it was just old stories dictated to him morning and evening. They mocked him openly: "What is with this messenger that he eats food and walks in the markets? Why was there not sent down to him an angel to be a warner with him - or a treasure dropped down to him, or a garden from which he could eat?"

Allah answered their arrogance with calm, undeniable wisdom:

• Human Messengers Are a Mercy and a Test: Every messenger before Muhammad (pbuh) also ate food and walked in the markets. Allah sent human prophets so people could follow a real, relatable human role model, and made people a test for one another to see who would remain patient.
• Why the Quran Was Revealed Gradually (Verse 32): The disbelievers also asked why the Quran was not sent down all at once. Allah explained the deep wisdom behind revealing it step by step over 23 years: "Thus [it is] that We may strengthen thereby your heart (O Muhammad), and We have spaced it distinctly." Classical scholars like Ibn Kathir explain that gradual revelation kept the Prophet's heart constantly comforted during hardships, answered real-life questions as they arose, and made the Quran easy for believers to memorize and put into practice.

deep_dives.title: Signs in Creation and the Barrier Between the Two Seas (Verses 45-54)
deep_dives.content:
Turning from history to the living world around us, Allah invites humanity to look closely at everyday miracles they take for granted.

The Tafsir Details: Allah points to the gentle stretching and shrinking of shadows guided by the sun, the night created as a peaceful garment of rest, the day made for rising and earning a living, and the winds sent ahead of His mercy to bring down pure rain that revives dead earth and gives water to countless humans and animals.

Then, in verse 53, Allah highlights an awe-inspiring natural wonder: "And it is He who has released the two seas, one fresh and sweet and one salty and bitter, and He placed between them a barrier (barzakh) and prohibiting partition." Just as Allah keeps fresh rivers and salty oceans from overtaking one another, He created every human being from water, establishing the sacred bonds of bloodline and marriage - reminding humanity that their Lord is All-Powerful.

deep_dives.title: The Grand Finale: The Servants of the Most Merciful ('Ibad ar-Rahman) and the Miracle of Repentance (Verses 63-77)
deep_dives.content:
Surah Al-Furqan concludes with one of the most beloved, uplifting passages in the entire Quran - describing the exact character of the true "Servants of the Most Merciful" ('Ibad ar-Rahman), alongside a breathtaking promise of forgiveness.

The Tafsir and Hadith Details: Allah paints a clear, practical portrait of His closest servants:

• Humility and Peace: They walk upon the earth gently and humbly, and when ignorant people address them harshly, they respond with peaceful words ("Salam"), refusing to sink into foolish arguments.
• Night Devotion: They spend parts of the night standing and prostrating to their Lord, praying to be spared the torment of Hellfire.
• Balanced Generosity: When they spend, they are neither wasteful nor stingy, keeping a wise middle path.
• Moral Purity and Avoiding Major Sins (Verse 68): They never call upon another god besides Allah, never kill a soul unjustly, and never commit unlawful sexual relations (zina).

Regarding verses 68-70, an authentic Hadith narrated by Ibn Abbas (RA) and recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari (4810) and Sahih Muslim (122) tells of a group of polytheists who had committed many murders and frequent zina in their past. They came to Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and said: "What you say and call to is truly good - if only you could tell us that there is an atonement for what we have done!"

Right then, Allah revealed the extraordinary promise of verse 70: "Except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous work. For them, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds (hasanat). And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful." Classical scholars explain that when a person sincerely repents, Allah not only wipes away their past sins - He transforms their bad record into good deeds and fills their life with righteous action!

The Surah finishes by describing how the 'Ibad ar-Rahman stay away from falsehood and vain gatherings, reflect deeply when reminded of Allah's verses, and make a timeless family prayer: "Our Lord, grant us from among our wives and offspring comfort to our eyes and make us a leader (example) for the righteous." For their patience, they are rewarded with the highest chambers of Paradise (Al-Ghurfah) and greeted with eternal peace.

Surah Al-Furqan carries the believer from the harsh mockery of Makkah and the tragic regret of Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt to the gentle, dignified character of 'Ibad ar-Rahman, reminding us that no matter how dark a person's past has been, Allah's mercy can turn sincere repentance into pure light and honor.
